source_row.rationale: ANA's position statement effective May 27, 2026 identifies nurse fatigue as a patient-safety and workforce-safety issue. It links long hours, heavy workload, inadequate staffing, and shiftwork with increased medical errors and calls for system-level strategies including appropriate staffing, realistic workloads, reasonable work hours, and contingency staffing plans. The item was reframed from a blanket legal claim about mandatory overtime to the supported fatigue/safety principle.
source_row.source_detail: ANA Position Statement, effective May 27, 2026: fatigue is a nurse and patient safety crisis; long hours, workload and inadequate staffing are linked to errors; employers and nurses share mitigation responsibilities.
source_row.source_name: American Nurses Association — Addressing Nurse Fatigue to Promote Health, Safety, and Well-Being for All
source_row.stem: A nurse is repeatedly scheduled for prolonged work hours because of chronic staffing shortages. Which patient-safety concern is most supported by current ANA guidance?
